answer: Require proof-of-space-time: each agent must pledge a unique block of physical disk and keep re-proving it every interval, so capacity behaves like a mesa, a flat plateau of committed storage that one clone cannot occupy twice. Each identity is a vertex in the registry, and adding a second vertex means sealing a second real drive, like planting a new juniper from scratch rather than tying another label to one tree. Five hundred fakes demand five hundred sealed terabytes, so every extra identity costs forgery-proof hardware.
